cards.text: Welcome in, friend. This book opens with the words of a man it calls the Teacher, a king in Jerusalem. And let me tell you, he does NOT ease into it.

cards.question: The Teacher is called the son of ___, king in Jerusalem.

cards.text: Then the Teacher cries out his very first words: futility of futilities, futility of futilities! He says it TWICE, in case somebody in the back missed it.

cards.question: Right away, the Teacher says only some things are futile.

cards.text: EVERYTHING, friend, and he doesn't even say good morning first. Then he asks a question about all the labor a man toils at under the sun.

cards.question: The Teacher looks at all the labor a person toils at under the sun. What does he ask about it?

answers.text: What a man gains from it
How long a man must keep at it
Who a man is working for

cards.text: Then he zooms WAY out and looks at people across time. Generations come, and generations go.

cards.question: While the generations come and go, the Teacher says the ___ remains forever.
Then the Teacher points up: the sun rises and the sun sets. What does he say it does after it sets?

answers.text: Hurries back to where it rises

cards.text: Then the Teacher turns to the wind, blowing southward and then turning northward. That wind has my sense of direction, friend.

cards.question: The Teacher watches the wind blow southward, then turn northward. What does he say it keeps doing?
All the rivers flow into the sea, and the Teacher says the sea finally fills up.
All the rivers flow into the sea. Where does the Teacher say the streams flow again?

answers.text: Back to the place they came from

cards.text: Then the Teacher says all things are wearisome, more than one can describe. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer counting dust, and I STILL couldn't describe it.

cards.question: The Teacher says all things are wearisome. He says the eye is not satisfied with seeing, and the ___ is not content with hearing.

cards.text: Then the Teacher looks at what has been and what has been done, and says it will all be done again. Stamp, bake, box, repeat: that's my whole week, and I LOVE it.

cards.question: The Teacher says there is nothing ___ under the sun.
Someone points at a thing and calls it new. The Teacher says it already existed in the ages before us.

cards.text: Then the Teacher says there is no remembrance of those who came before. Friend, after years in the back of a junk drawer, I don't need that one explained.

cards.question: The Teacher also talks about being remembered. He says people yet to come will be remembered by those who follow after them.

findings.problem: The blank asks for David, but card 1 gives no information from which the baker can reason out the Teacher's father. This asks for wording from a verse the baker has not seen rather than testing meaning they can infer.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This choice introduces the sun rising and setting in its own question. No earlier story card sets up Ecclesiastes 1:5; the preceding cards concern generations and the earth.

rule.text: The setup for a choice is on a story card. Not every choice card needs its own story card right before it: a choice card can follow another choice card when the setup is already told.

findings.problem: This choice introduces the rivers and the sea without a preceding story card setting up Ecclesiastes 1:7. The preceding story and choice concern the wind, so the rivers have not already been set up.
